findings.summary: Attribution is decided by content digest, not by path-set subtraction. UT-011 and UT-012 prove the case subtraction would have got wrong: a pre-existing dirty file modified again by the session still belongs to the session.
Unattributable paths raise SDD-V052 review warnings rather than passing silently. The fallback is the conservative direction.
ASES-0003 records no digests because it was created before the task that introduced them. It was not backfilled, so its own scope check reports review warnings rather than a clean result.
taskScope reads a test range such as UT-008 to UT-017 as two identifiers rather than ten, so a task naming a range records only its endpoints as required tests.

notes: APPROVE for the remediation as scoped: all ten required attribution cases pass, plus two more found during the work.
Reviewed under a distinct actor from the implementing session and the tester, per SDD-V051.
Two minor findings are recorded as CONV-008 and CONV-009 rather than fixed, because both need files outside the declared scope of TASK-012.
This is an AI review. It satisfies no human gate.
